We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON tree: root molecule, then reaction nodes each with template_id, children are precursor molecules (type mol). The route must be linear? At least 5 reactions, using those templates in that order. So we need to apply each template sequentially to break down the target into precursors, ending with some simple building blocks (maybe commercially available). We need to ensure each template is applicable; we attempted applying 29646 to target and got three possible outcomes (list of tuples). The result gave three possible product sets (precursors). The output format: apply_template returns tuple of tuples each containing SMILES strings of precursors? For first call, result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C',))"

So three possible disconnections. We need to pick one that can be further processed by next template 1914389, etc.

We need to construct a chain: target -> after template 29646 -> set of precursors (maybe two). Then each precursor may be further broken by next template? Usually retrosynthesis tree: each reaction node has children precursors; each precursor may be further expanded with next reaction. Since we need exactly 5 reactions in order, we can have a linear chain where each reaction takes the previous product as input and yields new precursors, but we need to keep using the same template order. So we can choose a single precursor path: each reaction reduces to a single precursor (or maybe multiple but we can keep only one branch). So we need to select a precursor from each step that can be processed by next template.

Let's examine the first template 29646 output options:

Option A: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" (has a silyl protecting group). Option B: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" (silyl on acid). Option C: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C" (no protecting group, simpler). Likely the later templates (1914389 etc.) were applied to the first or second? We previously applied 1914389 to the first option (with silyl) and got two precursors: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That seems promising: 1914389 splits into a core fragment and a side chain (maybe a protecting group). Then 1914390 applied to the core fragment gave "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". That's a further transformation.

Then 149040 applied to that gave no result (empty). But 149040 applied to the silyl-protected version gave a split into "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and "CC(C)(C)[Si](C)(C)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F". So 149040 seems to remove silyl group? Actually splits into core and silyl sulfonyl fluoride? Not sure.

We need to use templates in order: 29646, then 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

Thus we need to find a path where each subsequent template can be applied to a precursor from previous step.

Potential path:

Step1 (29646) on target -> choose precursor A: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" (call it P1).

Step2 (1914389) on P1 -> gave two precursors: core B = "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and side D = "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". We can continue with core B for next step.

Step3 (1914390) on core B -> gave "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". That's a product E.

Step4 (149040) on E gave no result earlier. But maybe 149040 should be applied to a different precursor, maybe the side D? Let's test 149040 on side D.
